\leanb{Log\allowbreak{}Der\allowbreak{}One} & There is $C$ such that $\bigl|\tfrac{L'}{L}(1,\chi)-\sum_\rho\tfrac1{1-\rho}\bigr|\le C\log 3q$ for every primitive $\chi$ modulo $q>1$, the sum over the zeros with $0<\re\rho<1$ and $\abs{\im\rho}\le1$. & special case & \cite{davenport1980multiplicative}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Elliptic\allowbreak{}Main\allowbreak{}Theorem\allowbreak{}CM} & The main theorem of complex multiplication for elliptic curves with CM by an imaginary quadratic field $K$, in idelic form: if $\sigma\in\mathrm{Aut}(\C/K)$ restricts to $\mathrm{Art}(s)$, then $\sigma$ transports an analytic uniformisation $\C/\mathfrak a\to E(\C)$ according to the finite part of $s$. & special case & \cite{shimura1971introduction,shimura1961complex}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Functional\allowbreak{}Equation} & For a unitary Hecke character $\chi$ of a totally complex field with non-zero infinity type relative to a CM type, the completed $L$-functions of $\chi$ and $\chi^{-1}$ exist and $\Lambda(s,\chi)=\varepsilon_\infty\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm f}(s)\,\Lambda(1-s,\chi^{-1})$. & special case & \cite{hecke1918neue,hecke1920neue,tate1967fourier}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hilbert\allowbreak{}Class\allowbreak{}Field\allowbreak{}J} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic, $K(j(\cO_K))$ is the Hilbert class field, of degree $h_K$; $j(\mathfrak a)=j(\mathfrak b)$ exactly when the ideal classes agree; and the $h_K$ values $j(\mathfrak a)$ are the conjugates of $j(\cO_K)$ over $K$. & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Partial\allowbreak{}Zeta\allowbreak{}Functional\allowbreak{}Equation} & For $F$ totally real of degree $n$ and ideal classes $C,C'$ whose product is the class of the different: $d_F^{s/2}\Gamma_\R(s)^n\zeta(s,C)=d_F^{(1-s)/2}\Gamma_\R(1-s)^n\zeta(1-s,C')$. & special case & \cite{hecke1917zetafunktion,tate1967fourier}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Deligne\allowbreak{}Ribet} & For $F$ totally real and a rational function $\varepsilon$ on narrow ray classes modulo $\ell^n$ that is $\ell$-integral: $L(1-k,\varepsilon)-N\mathfrak c^{k}L(1-k,\varepsilon(\mathfrak c\,\cdot))$ is $\ell$-integral, for $\mathfrak c$ prime to $\ell$ and $k\ge1$. & special case & \cite{deligne1980values,cassounogues1979valeurs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Klingen\allowbreak{}Deligne\allowbreak{}Ribet} & The preceding statement together with the theorem of Siegel and Klingen. & general & \cite{klingen1962werte,siegel1969berechnung,siegel1970fourierschen,deligne1980values,cassounogues1979valeurs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Join\allowbreak{}Out} & A conjunction of five statements internal to the archive, on critical values of Hecke $L$-functions of CM fields and on partial zeta values. & internal & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ht\allowbreak{}Card} & A comparison of Hodge--Tate weights. & general & \cite{fontaine1994semistables,fontaine1982certains}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ab\allowbreak{}Mul\allowbreak{}NSt} & An abelian variety of dimension $g$ over an algebraically closed field has exactly $n^{2g}$ points killed by $n$, for $n$ invertible in the field. & general & \cite{mumford1970abelian,weil1948varietes}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Abelian\allowbreak{}De\allowbreak{}Rham} & Five facts about the de Rham cohomology of an abelian scheme. & general & \cite{oda1969first,berthelot1982theorie,mazur1974universal}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{De\allowbreak{}Rham\allowbreak{}Pot\allowbreak{}Semistable} & Every continuous de Rham representation of the Galois group of a finite extension of $\Q_\ell$ is potentially semistable. & general & \cite{berger2002representations,andre2002filtrations,mebkhout2002analogue,kedlaya2004padic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Global\allowbreak{}Artin\allowbreak{}Reciprocity} & For every number field $E$ there is a homomorphism $\mathbb A_E^\times\to G_E^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with the properties of the global Artin map. & general & \cite{takagi1920theorie,artin1927beweis,chevalley1940theorie,tate1967global}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Hecke\allowbreak{}LAdic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}De\allowbreak{}Rham} & The $\ell$-adic character attached to an algebraic Hecke character is de Rham at every place above $\ell$, with Hodge--Tate weights given by the infinity type. & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1994semistables}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Algebraic\allowbreak{}Character\allowbreak{}WD} & Local--global compatibility for algebraic Hecke characters at every finite place, including those above $\ell$: the Weil--Deligne representation of the $\ell$-adic character at $w$ is the local component composed with the local Artin map. & general & \cite{serre1968abelian,fontaine1994potentiellement}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ar\allowbreak{}Calc} & Seven properties of arithmetic intersection numbers of Hermitian line bundles. & general & \cite{gillet1990arithmetic,bost1994heights}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ar\allowbreak{}Degree} & Two statements on arithmetic intersection numbers and Chern degrees. & variant & \cite{bost1994heights,gillet1990arithmetic,chern1946characteristic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Principalisation} & For a smooth projective integral variety over a field of characteristic $0$ and a non-zero ideal sheaf $I$: a sequence of blow-ups in smooth centres over the support of $I$ is an isomorphism away from the support and turns $I$ into an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings. & special case & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Arith\allowbreak{}Hilbert\allowbreak{}Samuel} & For a nef Hermitian line bundle $\bar L$ of arithmetic self-intersection $a$ on an arithmetic variety of relative dimension $D$, and any $\bar N$: the number of sections of $\bar L^{m}\otimes\bar N$ of sup-norm at most $1$ is finite for large $m$ and its logarithm is $\tfrac{a}{(D+1)!}m^{D+1}+o(m^{D+1})$. & general & \cite{gillet1992arithmetic,abbes1995theoreme,zhang1995positive,moriwaki2009continuity}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Automorphic\allowbreak{}Forms\allowbreak{}Finite\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a totally complex field, the automorphic forms on $\GL_a$ of a given level, $K_\infty$-type and infinitesimal character span a finite-dimensional space. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Base\allowbreak{}Change\allowbreak{}Isobaric\allowbreak{}Transfer} & Base change from a definite unitary group to an isobaric sum on $\GL_n$. & general & \cite{labesse2011changement}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Base\allowbreak{}Change\allowbreak{}Definite\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Group} & The same with the full induced product as local component. & general & \cite{labesse2011changement,bernstein1984pinvariant}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bernstein\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Irreducible} & Over a non-archimedean local field, the parabolically induced product of two irreducible unitarisable smooth representations of general linear groups is irreducible. & general & \cite{bernstein1984pinvariant}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bernstein\allowbreak{}Zelevinsky\allowbreak{}Finiteness} & For $\GL_n$ over a non-archimedean local field: irreducible smooth representations are admissible; Jacquet functors and parabolic induction preserve finite length; and induction commutes with the contragredient. & general & \cite{bernstein1976representations,bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bhatt\allowbreak{}Scholze\allowbreak{}Integral} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite, every lattice in a crystalline representation of $G_K$ is the \'etale realisation of a prismatic $F$-crystal on $\cO_K$, and the realisation is fully faithful. & general & \cite{bhatt2023prismatic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bhatt\allowbreak{}Scholze\allowbreak{}Crystalline\allowbreak{}Lattices} & The same for lattices with coefficients in the ring of integers of a finite extension of $\Q_\ell$. & general & \cite{bhatt2023prismatic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Bloch\allowbreak{}Kato\allowbreak{}Local} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite: the dimension formula for the Bloch--Kato subspace $H^1_f$ of a de Rham representation, and its duality with that of the Tate dual, rationally and integrally. & general & \cite{bloch1990lfunctions}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Borel\allowbreak{}Casselman} & For an admissible representation of $\GL_n$ over a non-archimedean local field, the Iwahori-fixed vectors map bijectively onto the fixed vectors of the Jacquet module. & general & \cite{borel1976admissible,casselman1980unramified}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Brauer\allowbreak{}Degree\allowbreak{}Zero} & For a representation $\rho$ of a finite group, $\chi_\rho-\dim\rho$ is an integral combination of differences $\mathrm{Ind}(\chi_i)-\mathrm{Ind}(1)$ with $\chi_i$ characters of degree one of subgroups. & general & \cite{brauer1947artin,deligne1973constantes}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{CMCurve\allowbreak{}Good\allowbreak{}Outside\allowbreak{}Prime\allowbreak{}St} & For a prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$, $p>3$, there is an elliptic curve over $\Q(j(\cO_K))$, $K=\Q(\sqrt{-p})$, with complex multiplication by $\cO_K$, good reduction outside $p$ and minimal discriminant $-p^3$. & general & \cite{gross1982minimal,gross1980arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Ess\allowbreak{}Square\allowbreak{}Integrable\allowbreak{}Segments} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, an irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_n$ is essentially square-integrable exactly when it is the quotient $L(\Delta)$ attached to a segment. & special case & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Converse\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$: two irreducible cuspidal representations of $\GL_n$, $n\ge2$, with the same Rankin--Selberg $\varepsilon$-constants against every irreducible representation of $\GL_{n-1}$ are isomorphic. & special case & \cite{henniart1993caracterisation}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Rec\allowbreak{}TExists} & At every finite place of a number field there is a map from the irreducible smooth representations of the groups $\GL_n$ to Weil--Deligne representations satisfying a stated list of laws of the local Langlands correspondence. & special case & \cite{harris2001geometry,henniart2000preuve,scholze2013local,bushnell2005essentially}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Pair\allowbreak{}UAlt} & For a CM field $E$ and a regular algebraic cuspidal representation $\pi$ of $\GL_a$ forming a polarised pair, there is a continuous semisimple $r\colon G_E\to\GL_a(\overline{\Q}_\ell)$ attached to $\pi$ with stated compatibilities. & variant & \cite{chenevier2013construction,shin2011galois,caraiani2012local,barnetlamb2012local,barnetlamb2014local,barnetlamb2014potential}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Forms\allowbreak{}Bounded\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a totally complex field, a cusp form on $\GL_a$ whose absolute value is invariant under the split centre is bounded. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1968automorphic,moeglin1994decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Jacquet\allowbreak{}Shalika\allowbreak{}Rigidity} & Over a totally complex field, two finite families of cuspidal automorphic representations of general linear groups whose isobaric sums have the same Satake parameters at almost all places coincide up to permutation. & special case & \cite{jacquet1981eulerI,jacquet1981eulerII}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Gelfand\allowbreak{}Kazhdan\allowbreak{}Dual} & Over a totally complex field, every cuspidal automorphic representation of $\GL_n$ is paired with itself twisted by $g\mapsto{}^{t}g^{-1}$. & variant & \cite{gelfand1975representations,bernstein1976representations,jacquet1981eulerII}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Generic\allowbreak{}Unlinked\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, every irreducible generic representation of $\GL_N$ is an irreducible product $L(\Delta_1)\times\dots\times L(\Delta_h)$ over pairwise unlinked segments. & special case & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Chevalley\allowbreak{}Units} & For a number field $E$ and $m,b>0$ there is $a>0$ prime to $b$ such that every unit congruent to $1$ modulo $a$ is an $m$-th power of a unit. & general & \cite{chevalley1951deux}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Geometric\allowbreak{}Lemma} & The geometric lemma of Bernstein and Zelevinsky for $\GL_n$ over a non-archimedean local field: the Jacquet module of an induced representation has a finite filtration by cell functors, with a statement on semisimplifications. & general & \cite{bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Grothendieck\allowbreak{}Ring\allowbreak{}Polynomial} & Over a non-archimedean local field, for any assignment $Z(\Delta)$ of segment classes, the Grothendieck group of finite-length representations of all $\GL_n$ is, with the induction product, the polynomial ring on the $Z(\Delta)$. & general & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Segment\allowbreak{}Representation} & Over a non-archimedean local field, the segment product $\sigma\times\sigma\nu\times\dots\times\sigma\nu^{l-1}$ of a cuspidal $\sigma$ has a unique irreducible subrepresentation, with Jacquet module $\sigma\otimes\sigma\nu\otimes\dots\otimes\sigma\nu^{l-1}$. & general & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,bernstein1977induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Zelevinsky\allowbreak{}Polynomial\allowbreak{}Ring} & Over a non-archimedean local field there are segment classes $Z(\Delta)$ and an isomorphism of the Grothendieck ring of the groups $\GL_n$ with $\Z[X_\Delta]$ sending $Z(\Delta)$ to $X_\Delta$. & general & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Depth\allowbreak{}Zero\allowbreak{}Induction} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$: if every member of the cuspidal support of an irreducible representation of $\GL_n$ has a non-zero vector fixed by the first congruence subgroup, so has the representation. & general & \cite{moy1994unrefined,moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Langlands\allowbreak{}Exhaustion\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_n$ is $L(\mathfrak m)$ for a multisegment $\mathfrak m$. & special case & \cite{silberger1978langlands,zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Langlands\allowbreak{}Multisegments} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$: the multisegment $\mathfrak m$ of $L(\mathfrak m)$ is unique, and $L(\mathfrak m+\mathfrak n)$ is a subquotient of $L(\mathfrak m)\times L(\mathfrak n)$. & general & \cite{zelevinsky1980induced,silberger1978langlands}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Standard\allowbreak{}Cosocle\allowbreak{}GL} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, a product of segment representations in standard order has a unique irreducible quotient. & special case & \cite{silberger1978langlands,zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Rec\allowbreak{}TExists} & The same statement as above, entered a second time in the file. & repeated & \cite{harris2001geometry,henniart2000preuve,scholze2013local,bushnell2005essentially}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Irreducible\allowbreak{}Admissible\allowbreak{}GL} & Every irreducible smooth complex representation of $\GL_n$ over a non-archimedean local field is admissible. & general & \cite{jacquet1975representations,bernstein1974all,bernstein1976representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Standard\allowbreak{}Functors\allowbreak{}Finite\allowbreak{}Length} & Over a non-archimedean local field, Jacquet functors and parabolic induction for block parabolic subgroups of $\GL_n$ preserve finite length. & general & \cite{bernstein1977induced,bernstein1976representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Tempered\allowbreak{}Product\allowbreak{}Of\allowbreak{}Square\allowbreak{}Integrable} & Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic $0$, an irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_N$ is tempered exactly when it is a product of square-integrable representations. & special case & \cite{jacquet1977generic,zelevinsky1980induced}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Casselman\allowbreak{}Wallach} & For a real unitary group and an irreducible unitary representation $\sigma$: every $(\mathfrak g,K)$-map from the $K$-finite vectors of $\sigma$ to a smooth Fr\'echet representation of moderate growth extends uniquely to a continuous map on smooth vectors. & special case & \cite{casselman1989canonical,wallach1983asymptotic,wallach1992real}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Chebotarev\allowbreak{}Degree\allowbreak{}One} & For a finite Galois extension $L/F$ of number fields, $g\in\Gal(L/F)$ and a finite set $S$ of primes, there is a prime outside $S$ of degree one over $\Q$, unramified in $L$, with Frobenius $g$. & special case & \cite{chebotarev1926bestimmung}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Chow\allowbreak{}Form\allowbreak{}Exists} & In characteristic $0$, a geometrically prime homogeneous ideal of dimension $D+1$ has a Chow form of degree equal to its Hilbert degree, unique up to a non-zero scalar. & special case & \cite{chow1937algebraischen}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Clozel\allowbreak{}Cohomological} & Over a totally complex field, every regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\GL_a$ is cohomological. & special case & \cite{clozel1990motifs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Clozel\allowbreak{}Purity} & Over a totally complex field, for a cuspidal representation of $\GL_a$ with algebraic infinitesimal characters there is an integer $w_0$ with $\mathrm{infChar}(\bar\tau)=w_0-\mathrm{infChar}(\tau)$ for every embedding $\tau$. & special case & \cite{clozel1990motifs}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Complex\allowbreak{}Multiplication\allowbreak{}JSt} & For $K$ imaginary quadratic there are a Hilbert class field $H\subset\C$ and an Artin isomorphism $\mathrm{Cl}(K)\cong\Gal(H/K)$ with $K(j(\mathfrak a))=H$ and $\mathrm{art}([\mathfrak b])\,j(\mathfrak a)=j(\mathfrak b^{-1}\mathfrak a)$. & general & \cite{hasse1927neue,shimura1971introduction}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Bounded} & On the adelic unitary group of a Hermitian space over a CM field, a smooth cuspidal automorphic function all of whose derivatives have uniform moderate growth is bounded, with all its derivatives. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1968automorphic,moeglin1994decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Decay\allowbreak{}Bound} & On the same group, a quantitative form: for a given level and exponents, finitely many derivatives bound $\abs{\varphi(g)}\,\mathrm{ht}(g)^N$ for every cusp function of that level. & special case & \cite{moeglin1994decomposition,harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Decay\allowbreak{}Sobolev} & On the same group, the rapid-decay seminorms of a cusp function of given level are bounded by its Sobolev seminorms of moderate growth. & variant & \cite{moeglin1994decomposition,harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Rapid\allowbreak{}Decay} & On the same group, every smooth cuspidal automorphic function of uniform moderate growth decays rapidly. & special case & \cite{gelfand1969representation,harishchandra1968automorphic,moeglin1994decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cusp\allowbreak{}Trace\allowbreak{}Class} & On the same group, for every smooth compactly supported $f$ the operator $R_{\mathrm{cusp}}(f)$ on the cuspidal $L^2$-space is of trace class. & special case & \cite{gelfand1969representation,dixmier1978factorisations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cuspidal\allowbreak{}Mirabolic} & For every finite field, $\GL_{n+1}$ has an irreducible cuspidal complex representation, and the restriction of such a representation to the mirabolic subgroup is the induced representation of a non-degenerate character. & general & \cite{green1955characters,gelfand1970representations,zelevinsky1981representations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cuspidal\allowbreak{}Spectrum\allowbreak{}GL} & For $\GL_a$ over a totally complex field: the cuspidal part of $L^2$ is a Hilbert direct sum of irreducible subrepresentations, with statements on their finite vectors and on boundedness of cusp forms. & special case & \cite{gelfand1963automorphic,godement1966spectral,harishchandra1968automorphic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cycle\allowbreak{}Heights} & Arithmetic heights and arithmetic intersection functionals exist, are multilinear in mixed arguments, and satisfy a projection formula for heights. & general & \cite{gillet1990arithmetic,bost1994heights}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Depth\allowbreak{}Zero\allowbreak{}Jacquet\allowbreak{}Injective} & Over a non-archimedean local field, for an irreducible representation of $\GL_n$ and a standard parabolic subgroup: a vector fixed by the first congruence subgroup and by the integral points of the unipotent radical, whose image in the Jacquet module is zero, is zero. & special case & \cite{moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Depth\allowbreak{}Zero\allowbreak{}Support} & Over a non-archimedean local field, if an irreducible representation of $\GL_n$ has a non-zero vector fixed by the first congruence subgroup, so has every member of its cuspidal support. & special case & \cite{moy1994unrefined,moy1996jacquet}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Classification} & For the real unitary groups $\U(p,q)$: every Harish-Chandra parameter carries an irreducible unitary square-integrable representation with that infinitesimal character and a unique lowest $K$-type, with stated uniqueness. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1965discrete,harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Cover} & For the double cover of $\U(p,q)$ defined by a square root of the determinant: the discrete series is a family $D(\lambda)$ indexed by parameters, with prescribed $K$-types, and every discrete series representation is equivalent to one of them. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1965discrete,harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Cover\allowbreak{}Exists} & For that double cover and every parameter $\lambda$ there is a discrete series representation with parameter $\lambda$. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Exists} & The same as \lean{DiscreteSeriesUpqExists} below. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Hermitian\allowbreak{}Unique} & Two discrete series representations of $\U(p,q)$ with the same Harish-Chandra parameter, transported to the unitary group of a Hermitian matrix by two frames, are unitarily equivalent. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Lowest\allowbreak{}KType} & In a discrete series representation of $\U(p,q)$ with Harish-Chandra parameter $\lambda$, the $K$-type of highest weight $\lambda+\rho_n-\rho_c$ occurs with multiplicity one, with a second clause on its uniqueness. & special case & \cite{schmid1975some,harishchandra1966discrete}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Discrete\allowbreak{}Series\allowbreak{}Upq\allowbreak{}Exists} & For every Harish-Chandra parameter $\lambda$ of $\U(p,q)$ there is an irreducible unitary representation with square-integrable matrix coefficients that contains the $K$-type $\lambda+\rho_n-\rho_c$, with a clause on its other $K$-types. & special case & \cite{harishchandra1966discrete,schmid1975some}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Dixmier\allowbreak{}Malliavin\allowbreak{}Factorisation} & For a group closed in $\GL_n(\C)$ with a Haar measure, every smooth compactly supported function is a finite sum of convolutions of two such functions, the first supported in a prescribed neighbourhood of the identity. & special case & \cite{dixmier1978factorisations}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Eisenstein\allowbreak{}Continuation} & For a Hermitian space $V$ of positive rank over a CM extension, the Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled group $\U(V\oplus-V)$ attached to a section of the degenerate principal series continues meromorphically, with poles of finite order. & special case & \cite{langlands1976functional,moeglin1994decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Doubling\allowbreak{}Method\allowbreak{}Local\allowbreak{}Zeta\allowbreak{}Integrals} & The preceding statement together with the basic identity of the doubling method. & variant & \cite{gelbart1987explicit,langlands1976functional}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Flath\allowbreak{}Tensor\allowbreak{}Product} & Every irreducible unitary representation of the adelic unitary group of a Hermitian space over a CM extension is a restricted tensor product of irreducible unitary representations of the local groups. & special case & \cite{flath1979decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unitary\allowbreak{}Irreducible\allowbreak{}Admissible} & Every irreducible unitary representation of a non-archimedean local unitary group of that kind is admissible. & special case & \cite{bernstein1974all}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Flath\allowbreak{}Factorisation} & The factorisation of \lean{FlathTensorProduct}, with the local factors unramified at almost all places. & special case & \cite{flath1979decomposition}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Fontaine\allowbreak{}Bcris} & Seven properties of Fontaine's ring $B_{\mathrm{cris}}$, among them injectivity of Frobenius and of $B_{\mathrm{cris}}\to B_{\mathrm{dR}}$ and the fundamental exact sequence. & general & \cite{fontaine1982certains,fontaine1994corps,fontaine1994semistables}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]

\leanb{Weyl\allowbreak{}Branching} & The restriction to $\GL_n(\C)$, and to $\U(n)$, of the irreducible representation of $\GL_{n+1}(\C)$ of highest weight $\lambda$ is the multiplicity-free sum over the weights interlacing $\lambda$. & general & \cite{weyl1946classical}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Dual\allowbreak{}Abelian\allowbreak{}Scheme} & Every abelian scheme has a dual abelian scheme of the same relative dimension, with a Poincar\'e bundle exhibiting each as the dual of the other. & general & \cite{mumford1965geometric,faltings1990degeneration}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Zarhin\allowbreak{}Statement} & Over the valuation ring of an algebraically closed non-archimedean field, an abelian scheme with a relatively ample line bundle is a retract of a principally polarised one. & special case & \cite{zarhin1977endomorphisms,moretbailly1985pinceaux}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Fargues\allowbreak{}Exact} & For a $p$-divisible group over the ring of integers of a complete algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$: the kernel of the Hodge--Tate map is the annihilator, under the pairing induced by the Weil pairing, of the corresponding part of the dual. & general & \cite{fargues2008isomorphisme,tate1967pdivisible}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Nef\allowbreak{}RR} & An asymptotic Riemann--Roch statement for a divisor class that is nef on the generic fibre of an arithmetic variety: $D!\,\dim H^0(\tau a)/\tau^{D}$ tends to the generic degree. & special case & \cite{lazarsfeld2004positivity,kleiman1966toward}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Poincare\allowbreak{}Lelong\allowbreak{}Inv} & A Poincar\'e--Lelong formula on an arithmetic variety: the integral of $\log\norm{s}$ against Chern forms equals a sum over the horizontal components of the divisor of $s$, with a correction. & special case & \cite{lelong1957integration,bost1994heights}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Principalisation\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}Zero} & For a smooth separated quasi-compact scheme over a field of characteristic $0$, an ideal sheaf and a divisor with simple normal crossings: a sequence of blow-ups in smooth centres having normal crossings with the divisor makes the ideal an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings. & general & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII,kollar2007lectures}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Resolution\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}Zero} & Every reduced separated scheme of finite type over a field of characteristic $0$ has a resolution by a sequence of blow-ups that is an isomorphism over the smooth locus, the preimage of the singular locus being a divisor with simple normal crossings. & general & \cite{hironaka1964resolution,hironaka1964resolutionII,kollar2007lectures}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Cheb} & For a number field $F$, an open normal subgroup $U$ of $G_F$, $g\in G_F$ and a finite set of primes: there is a prime outside the set, of degree one and unramified over $\Q$, with inertia in $U$ and a Frobenius in $gU$. & special case & \cite{chebotarev1926bestimmung}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Eis\allowbreak{}BL} & Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled unitary group attached to standard sections converge in a half-plane and continue meromorphically, with poles of finite order. & special case & \cite{bernstein2024meromorphic,langlands1976functional}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Std} & The Siegel--Weil formula for a definite Hermitian or skew-Hermitian space: the Siegel Eisenstein series is holomorphic at $s_0=(m-n)/2$ and its value there is a constant times the theta integral. & general & \cite{weil1965formule,ichino2007siegel,yamana2011siegel}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Matching} & A statement in the archive's own terms: theta integrals attached to matched data agree up to explicit constants. & internal & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Global\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ over a number field unramified outside $S$: Tate's global Euler characteristic formula. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,milne1986arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Global\allowbreak{}Finiteness} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ as above: $H^0$, $H^1$ and $H^2$ are finite and the higher groups vanish for $\ell\ne2$. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,milne1986arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: Tate's local Euler characteristic formula. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Finiteness} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: $H^0$, $H^1$ and $H^2$ are finite and the higher groups vanish. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Duality} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a finite place: Tate local duality. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Greenberg\allowbreak{}Wiles} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ and local conditions: the formula of Greenberg and Wiles comparing a Selmer group with the dual Selmer group. & general & \cite{wiles1995modular,darmon1995fermat}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Unramified\allowbreak{}Orthogonality} & For a finite $\ell^r$-torsion Galois module $M$ at a place not above $\ell$ where $M$ is unramified: the unramified classes of $M$ and of its Tate dual are exact annihilators. & general & \cite{serre1964cohomologie,milne1986arithmetic,tate1963duality}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Siegel\allowbreak{}Weil\allowbreak{}Unitary\allowbreak{}Convergent} & For a non-degenerate Hermitian form of rank $M$ over a CM extension: $[\U(J)]$ has finite volume, and for $2n<M$ the mean of the theta series of frames with a given Gram matrix is the product of the local densities. & general & \cite{siegel1935analytische,braun1941theorie,weil1965formule,borel1962arithmetic}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Euler\allowbreak{}Char\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite and a finite continuous $\ell^r$-torsion module: $\#H^1=\#H^0\cdot\#H^2\cdot\#M^{[K:\Q_\ell]}$. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Finiteness\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite and such a module: $H^0$, $H^1$, $H^2$ are finite and $H^n=0$ for $n\ge3$. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Local\allowbreak{}Tate\allowbreak{}Duality\allowbreak{}K} & For $K/\Q_\ell$ finite: $H^2(G_K,\mu_{\ell^r})\cong\Z/\ell^r$ and the cup-product pairings with the Tate dual are perfect. & general & \cite{tate1963duality,serre1964cohomologie}\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\leanb{Every\allowbreak{}Character} & The conclusion: $L(s,\chi)\ne0$ for every Dirichlet character $\chi$ and every $s$ with $\re s>\tfrac12$, $s=1$ excluded for trivial $\chi$. The file returns it under the hypothesis of \cref{st:vwin}. & conclusion & ---\\
\addlinespace[1pt]
\end{longtable}}
